I'm sure you have all heard of ChatGPT by now. It has become a buzzword within days of its release and professionals in all fields, especially in high skilled areas like lawyers, doctors, engineers are questioning whether such AI can actually replace them and work.

So in this video I want to talk about what ChatGPT is and how it even popped up, talk a bit about the organization behind GPT called "OpenAI", which has already created many other machine learning models besides Chat GPT and also explain technically about all that.
And then we'll dive in and actually put ChatGPT to use for some DevOps related tasks.
I really want to see how it can help in generating configuration code for building DevOps processes or different parts of those processes and how well it knows different DevOps technologies, but not just some shallow examples or boilerplate code that I can get from official documentation, but instead also try more fine-tuning and small optimizations in that configuration code.

We're also going to check out an open source command line tool that is built on top of ChatGPT and was specifically created for engineers to generate infrastructure as code templates and more and finally we'll talk about the impact of ChatGPT, the quality and usefulness of such a tool for engineers and whether it will really replace the engineers and to what extent you should be concerned.

About the Course
Edureka’s DevOps online training is designed to help you master key tools of Devops lifecycle like Docker, Puppet, Jenkins, Nagios, GIT, Ansible, SaltStack and Chef used by a DevOps Engineer for automating multiple steps in SDLC. During this course, our expert DevOps instructors will help you:

Edureka’s DevOps online training is designed to help you master key tools of Devops lifecycle like Docker, Puppet, Jenkins, Nagios, GIT, Ansible, SaltStack and Chef used by a DevOps Engineer for automating multiple steps in SDLC. During this course, our expert DevOps instructors will help you:

videoDescription:

In this interview tips training tutorial, Richard McMunn will cover:

1. A list of DEVOPS interview questions I recommend you prepare for;
2. Example ANSWERS to help you PASS your DevOps Engineer interview;
3. The QUALITIES you MUST demonstrate during your DevOps interview;
4. Further resources to help you PASS your DevOps Engineer interview!

HERE'S A FULL LIST OF DEVOPS ENGINEER INTERVIEW QUESTIONS
Q1. Tell me about yourself and why you want to work in this DevOps role?
Q2. What are the most important skills and qualities needed to work as a DevOps Engineer?

Q9. What does DevOps mean to you and what is its purpose in our organization?

Q16. Explain how you copy a local file to HDFS?
Q17. Describe how you would make a background process run?

Q19. Talk me through the process of what happens when someone accesses a URL via a web browser?

videoTitle: Will AI replace DevOps Engineer? AI tools in DevOps 2024
videoDescription:
AI for DevOps | Will AI replace DevOps engineers | DevOps AI tools
In this DevOps video we will learning How AI and ML can be used in DevOps tasks like CICD, Monitoring, Logging, Deployments and more.
Along with Popular AI tools in devops and companies using AI with Devops.

Connect with me on LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/nasiullha-chaudhari/ 

AI and DevOps are two fascinating fields in the tech world, and they're coming together in exciting ways. Many companies are exploring how AI can help improve their DevOps practices to make things smoother and more efficient.

With AI, we can automate repetitive tasks, optimize resource usage, and make better decisions.

A common question is whether AI will replace DevOps or the engineers working in this area. Well, AI can certainly enhance DevOps, but it won't replace the people. Instead, it will work alongside skilled DevOps engineers to make things even better.

Timestamps
Intro 0"00
Eminem Featuring 0:50
DevOps Tasks that AI can replace 01:20
Popular AI tools in DevOps 03:25
Companies using AI in DevOps 04:40
How Netflix AI with DevOps 04:48
How Google uses AI in Devops 04:58
How LinkedIn uses AI for DevOps 05:16
Problems when using AI for DevOps 05:47
Outro 07:26

The GitLab Developer Survey, available at https://about.gitlab.com/developer-survey/ 

AI Tools for DevOps:
1. Splunk
2. Harness
3. Amazon CodeGuru
4. PagerDuty
5. Dynatrace
6. Datadog
7. AppDynamics
8. Opsani
9. Puppet
10. Chef

These AI-powered tools, combined with popular DevOps platforms, enable organizations to accelerate their software development and delivery processes while ensuring greater reliability, scalability, and performance. The integration of AI in DevOps brings innovative solutions to complex challenges, allowing teams to focus on creating value for their customers.

1. Netflix: Netflix is well-known for its use of AI and machine learning to optimize content delivery, personalization, and infrastructure management in their DevOps workflows.
2. Google: Google has been a pioneer in AI research and has integrated AI tools and technologies into their DevOps processes to improve system performance and operational efficiency.
3. Facebook: Facebook uses AI and machine learning algorithms to optimize infrastructure, manage user data, and streamline their continuous deployment practices in DevOps.
4. Amazon: Amazon's AWS offers various AI-powered DevOps tools and services, such as Amazon CodeGuru, AWS CodePipeline, and AWS CodeDeploy, to help developers automate tasks and improve software delivery.
5. Microsoft: Microsoft uses AI in their DevOps workflows to optimize Azure services, automate infrastructure management, and enhance developer productivity.
6. Spotify: Spotify uses AI-driven analytics and monitoring tools to gain insights into application performance and user behavior, enabling continuous improvements in their DevOps practices.
7. Twitter: Twitter employs AI and machine learning for infrastructure management, incident detection, and performance optimization in their DevOps pipelines.
8. Uber: Uber utilizes AI to manage large-scale infrastructure, improve data analysis
9. Airbnb: Airbnb leverages AI to optimize their continuous deployment and delivery pipelines
10. IBM: IBM has integrated AI technologies into their DevOps tools and solutions, such as IBM Cloud Pak for Applications, to facilitate intelligent automation and faster software delivery.

Adoption of AI in DevOps is not limited to these companies alone. More and more companies are embracing AI in their DevOps processes. By doing so, they can reduce manual work, spot issues faster, and deliver higher-quality software to their customers.

In conclusion, AI and DevOps make a fantastic team. They bring exciting possibilities for the future of software development, making it more efficient and effective. Embracing AI in DevOps can give your company a competitive edge in the tech world. So, let's welcome this exciting partnership!

videoTitle: Guided DevOps Meditation
videoDescription:
Dive into a unique meditative experience designed specifically for the DevOps Engineer. In the hustle of ensuring seamless deployments and system operations, every DevOps professional deserves a moment to reboot, refresh, and recenter.

Whether you're in the midst of a complex project or wrapping up a day of successful deployments, this meditation will guide you to find serenity amidst the codes and systems.

🔗 Find tranquility amidst the binaries. Hit play and embark on a journey to the calm side of DevOps.

Don't forget to LIKE, SHARE, and SUBSCRIBE for more content dedicated to the DevOps community! 🚀👍

▬▬▬▬▬▬ S C R I P T  📜  ▬▬▬▬▬▬

"Begin by finding a serene place where you can sit undisturbed. As you prepare to delve into a state of calm, think of it as setting up the perfect environment for a seamless deployment."

"Sit or lie down in a comfortable position, ensuring that your back is straight and your hands rest lightly on your lap or by your sides. Close your eyes gently. Let's begin our system reboot."

"Start by taking a deep breath in, inhaling calmness and clarity, like the smooth initiation of a well-planned product. And exhale, releasing any system glitches or unwanted bugs from your mind."

"Imagine your mind as a server room. Each server represents a thought or a responsibility in your life. Some servers are humming busily, while others are quiet and in standby mode."

"Visualize a cooling system, a gust of fresh, clean air entering the room, stabilizing the temperature. This cooling breath ensures that every server, every thought, operates at its peak without overheating."

"As you continue breathing deeply, bring to mind a continuous integration and continuous deployment pipeline. With every inhale, new features and positive affirmations are integrated. With every exhale, new code is deployed to production."

"Imagine a monitoring dashboard, showcasing green status indicators. Your body is this system. Your heart rate, your breathing, your state of calm are all in optimal state - all systems operational and running smoothly."

"Think about the code commits. Sometimes, errors occur, and that's okay. Acknowledge them without judgment, fix them, and move on. For now, release any attachment to those errors, letting them float away like logs being archived."

"Your breathing is now your main server, your central command. Focus on its rhythm, the gentle in-and-out, the same predictable yet vital process, akin to the regular checks and balances in DevOps."

"Even in the face of challenges, remember that every system has its recovery procedure. Your mind, your spirit, and your body are no different. You have the resilience, the backup plans, and the capability for recovery."

"Slowly begin to transition, like smoothly moving from development to production. Become aware of your surroundings. Feel the chair or the floor supporting you, the gentle rhythm of your heart."

"When you're ready, with the confidence of a successful code deployment, open your eyes. As you go back into the world, remember that just like in DevOps, balance, continuous improvement, and adaptation are key."

videoTitle: 😱Hey DevOps, you’re killing my job 😢!
videoDescription:
😱Hey DevOps, you’re killing my job 😢!
Really? No 😉.
Don't panic and check out the talk 🎞 I had with Pia Wiedermayer on this topic.

Is DevOps really the reason why testing and quality assurance (QA) employees are being increasingly automated out of a job?
Pia Wiedermayer, Head of QA, and Romano Roth, Head of DevOps, discuss different ways to incorporate the wealth of experience of testing and QA specialists into the agile team culture.

Insight: 
- DevOps is often equated with automation
- What does this mean for people in these roles and with these responsibilities?
- Testers offer a wealth of experience that can be incorporated into the
agile team culture

Software testing and quality assurance are changing. Topics such as agility, DevOps and automation strongly influence existing roles and areas of responsibility in software quality assurance as well as during the entire software life cycle. Standard testing and QA roles no longer exist in many (project) organisations. Dedicated testing teams are increasingly a thing of the past.

What does this mean for people in these roles and with these responsibilities? Is there no room for them anymore? Are their skills and expertise no longer needed?

DevOps is often equated with automation. Is DevOps responsible for automating employees out of a job? What is behind the hype and who or what is DevOps actually?

Pia Wiedermayer, Head of Quality Assurance https://www.linkedin.com/in/piawiedermayer/, and Romano Roth, Head of DevOps, at Zühlke Switzerland tackle these questions. They talk about the challenges in their projects, examine roles and tasks and reveal new paths for professional and personal development. They also discuss ways to incorporate the wealth of experience of testers into the agile team culture and whether automation is the new testing.

videoTitle: ♾️🛠️CI/CD Pipeline Explained in Tamil🔁 | #thillaithetechie
videoDescription:
✅ Continuous Integration (CI):
✅ CI is a development practice where code changes are automatically built, tested, and integrated into a shared repository multiple times a day.
✅ It ensures early detection of integration errors and promotes collaboration among developers by providing rapid feedback on code changes.

✅ Continuous Delivery (CD):
✅ CD extends CI by automating the deployment process, enabling teams to release software changes to production or staging environments quickly and reliably.
✅ It streamlines the deployment pipeline, reduces manual intervention, and enhances the consistency and repeatability of software releases.

✅ Pipeline Automation:
✅ CI/CD pipelines automate various stages of the software delivery process, including code compilation, testing, artifact creation, and deployment.
✅ Automated pipelines ensure consistency, efficiency, and reliability, allowing teams to focus on delivering value-added features and improvements.

✅ Feedback Loop:
✅ CI/CD pipelines incorporate feedback loops at each stage, enabling teams to identify and address issues promptly, iterate on solutions, and continuously improve software quality and performance.

✅ DevOps Culture:
✅ CI/CD practices are integral to the DevOps culture, fostering collaboration between development and operations teams, breaking down silos, and promoting a culture of continuous improvement and innovation.

videoTitle: 😱Hey DevOps, you’re killing my job 😢!
videoDescription:
😱Hey DevOps, you’re killing my job 😢!
Really? No 😉.
Don't panic and check out the talk 🎞 I had with Pia Wiedermayer on this topic.

Is DevOps really the reason why testing and quality assurance (QA) employees are being increasingly automated out of a job?
Pia Wiedermayer, Head of QA, and Romano Roth, Head of DevOps, discuss different ways to incorporate the wealth of experience of testing and QA specialists into the agile team culture.

Insight: 
- DevOps is often equated with automation
- What does this mean for people in these roles and with these responsibilities?
- Testers offer a wealth of experience that can be incorporated into the
agile team culture

Software testing and quality assurance are changing. Topics such as agility, DevOps and automation strongly influence existing roles and areas of responsibility in software quality assurance as well as during the entire software life cycle. Standard testing and QA roles no longer exist in many (project) organisations. Dedicated testing teams are increasingly a thing of the past.

What does this mean for people in these roles and with these responsibilities? Is there no room for them anymore? Are their skills and expertise no longer needed?

DevOps is often equated with automation. Is DevOps responsible for automating employees out of a job? What is behind the hype and who or what is DevOps actually?

Pia Wiedermayer, Head of Quality Assurance https://www.linkedin.com/in/piawiedermayer/, and Romano Roth, Head of DevOps, at Zühlke Switzerland tackle these questions. They talk about the challenges in their projects, examine roles and tasks and reveal new paths for professional and personal development. They also discuss ways to incorporate the wealth of experience of testers into the agile team culture and whether automation is the new testing.

videoTitle: C'est quoi le DevOps ? Tout comprendre en deux minutes ! CI/CD, feedback et qualité !
videoDescription:
De manière triviale, le DevOps est la contraction de développement et d'opérationnel. 

Au délà d'être une méthode, c'est avant tout une culture de l'amélioration continue ancrée dans les pratiques agiles.

videoTitle: ♾️🛠️CI/CD Pipeline Explained in Tamil🔁 | #thillaithetechie
videoDescription:
✅ Continuous Integration (CI):
✅ CI is a development practice where code changes are automatically built, tested, and integrated into a shared repository multiple times a day.
✅ It ensures early detection of integration errors and promotes collaboration among developers by providing rapid feedback on code changes.

✅ Continuous Delivery (CD):
✅ CD extends CI by automating the deployment process, enabling teams to release software changes to production or staging environments quickly and reliably.
✅ It streamlines the deployment pipeline, reduces manual intervention, and enhances the consistency and repeatability of software releases.

✅ Pipeline Automation:
✅ CI/CD pipelines automate various stages of the software delivery process, including code compilation, testing, artifact creation, and deployment.
✅ Automated pipelines ensure consistency, efficiency, and reliability, allowing teams to focus on delivering value-added features and improvements.

✅ Feedback Loop:
✅ CI/CD pipelines incorporate feedback loops at each stage, enabling teams to identify and address issues promptly, iterate on solutions, and continuously improve software quality and performance.

✅ DevOps Culture:
✅ CI/CD practices are integral to the DevOps culture, fostering collaboration between development and operations teams, breaking down silos, and promoting a culture of continuous improvement and innovation.

videoTitle: InFocus - Honeycomb: Post-Merge Control #LaunchDarkly #FeatureFlags #DevOps
videoDescription:
After a merger, things can get messy fast.

For us, LaunchDarkly became the way to get control back, especially once real customers were on the line.

It’s not about hoping changes work. It’s about knowing you can flip a switch, roll things back, and stay in control when production gets unpredictable.
channelDescription:
LaunchDarkly is the runtime control layer for the AI era. For over a decade we have helped engineering teams control what ships in production, from feature flags to full release governance. Today that mission extends to the AI agents and code that are increasingly building, modifying, and operating software on behalf of engineering teams.

With CodeControl and AgentControl, teams can ship faster, govern what runs in production, and automatically respond when something needs to change, without waiting on a redeploy. LaunchDarkly runs on infrastructure that handles over 50 trillion flag evaluations a day, which means the same platform that governs your features also governs your agents.

Founded in 2014 by Edith Harbaugh and John Kodumal, LaunchDarkly has been named on the Forbes Cloud 100 list and serves some of the most demanding engineering teams in the world.

Learn more at launchdarkly.com

videoTitle: Intro to DevOps | AZ-400 | Episode 1
videoDescription:
Episode 1 of 25
For the full video series, click here: https://aka.ms/AZ-400onYouTube

In this episode, Microsoft Technical Trainer Andrew Conniff introduces Module 01: Introduction to DevOps. You’ll explore DevOps as the union of people, process, and products to enable continuous delivery of value, and learn why continuous improvement and cycle-time optimization are essential in modern software delivery.

The session covers the fundamentals of Git repositories, branching workflows, pull requests, collaboration, and code review. You’ll also examine key DevOps practices, including CI/CD, monitoring and logging, cloud fundamentals, infrastructure as code, microservices, and containers. The episode concludes with an overview of Azure DevOps (Boards, Pipelines, Repos, Artifacts, Test Plans) and GitHub (Repositories, Codespaces, Actions, Packages, and security features) and how they support end-to-end DevOps workflows aligned to AZ-400 certification objectives.

Learn more about this course and take the certification exam to test your new skills: https://aka.ms/AZ-400onLearn

videoTitle: BTAIH E03 · Mohamed Daoudi, DevOps Engineer · Can AI Replace DevOps Engineers?
videoDescription:
My third guest on BTAIH is Mohamed Daoudi, a DevOps engineer whose path took him from ENSA and self-taught Linux and Docker to early-stage companies, large-scale cloud systems at Oracle, and independent consulting.

We get into what happens when AI stops being a chatbot and starts touching real infrastructure: writing scripts, handling repetitive migrations, executing commands, configuring CI/CD, connecting hosting and domains, and helping ship a working website in less than 24 hours.

It is a practical conversation, not a hype one. Where AI genuinely makes a DevOps engineer faster, where it turns 100 lines into 10,000, and why giving an agent access to your systems is only useful when you still understand the infrastructure underneath it.

About Mohamed

Mohamed Daoudi is a DevOps engineer with experience across startups, service companies, Oracle Cloud and independent consulting. His work has included CI/CD, Kubernetes, cloud infrastructure, incident management and keeping production systems stable at scale.

Or, at other times, it's working with data formats like JSON or YAML.

videoDescription:
Set up a complete D365 F&O project from scratch. Learn to configure Lifecycle Services (LCS), Azure DevOps, and a local development VM.

───────────

38:48 → Running the Self-Signed Certificate PowerShell Script
39:30 → Running the Admin User Provisioning Tool
40:14 → Accessing F&O Locally via IIS
41:29 → Recap

──────────────
💡 What You'll Learn
──────────────

✓ How to provision a new Lifecycle Services (LCS) implementation project.
✓ Configure Azure DevOps for D365 (including TFVC & Classic Pipeline settings).
✓ The critical step of connecting LCS to Azure DevOps for integration.
✓ How to deploy and access a local development VHD using Hyper-V.
✓ Authenticate the local VM using Azure App Registration.

──────────────────────────
🚀 About This D365 Development Series
──────────────────────────

This series goes beyond basic tutorials to show you how real-world Dynamics 365 (D365FO) projects are built from start to finish. We'll build a complete, end-to-end "Automated Customer Tiering System" for a fictional client, Bluestone Industrial Components (BIC).

You'll see every step of a production-ready solution, from setup to deployment, covering:
➤ Core X++ Development: Extending tables and forms (CustTable), creating Enums, and implementing custom business logic using Chain of Command (CoC).
➤ Automation: Building robust, automated batch jobs with the SysOperation Framework.
➤ APIs & Integration: Creating Data Entities to build secure OData REST APIs and for Data Management Framework (DMF) exports.
➤ Event-Driven Architecture: Firing real-time alerts from D365 to Azure Logic Apps using Business Events.
➤ Business Intelligence: Connecting D365 to Power BI to build an interactive sales dashboard.
➤ DevOps & ALM: Setting up a complete CI/CD pipeline in Azure DevOps, managing source control (TFVC), and automating builds.

────────────────
💻 Tools & Technologies
────────────────

🔹Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations (D365FO)
🔹X++
🔹Visual Studio 2019
🔹Lifecycle Services (LCS)
🔹Azure DevOps (ADO)
🔹SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS)
🔹Power BI Desktop
🔹Azure Logic Apps

───────────────────
💬 Feedback & Future Topics
───────────────────

This series covers the core components of a practical, end-to-end D365 project. I know there are many more topics we could dive into, from advanced debugging to complex form patterns.

I welcome your feedback and ideas! If there's a specific D365 topic you'd like to see covered in a future video, please share your suggestions in the comments section below.

videoTitle: DKT97 | DevOps в 2026: Platform Engineering, AI-агенты и будущее джунов
videoDescription:
Состояние DevOps в 2026: Platform Engineering, AI-агенты и что стало с junior-инженерами. Собрались на кухне с тимлидом системного юнита из большой компании - поговорить что и как сейча.

О ЧЁМ ВЫПУСК
• DevOps vs SRE в 2026: где проходит граница и почему «you build it, you run it» иногда создаёт больше проблем, чем решает.
• War story: упавший Kubernetes во время корпоратива с пивом - классика первых K8s-внедрений.
• Момент, когда DevOps ломается: 600 сервисов, 3600 пайплайнов и почему каждый новый инженер пишет 3601-й.
• Platform Engineering: зачем нужна платформа, что такое метаплатформы и как устроены слои внутри крупной компании.
• Junior + AI = middle: что изменилось с приходом AI-ассистентов и сколько теперь занимает обучение DevOps.
• AI в работе DevOps прямо сейчас: мультиагентные помощники для расследования инцидентов, внутренние vs внешние модели.
• Реальные AI-катастрофы 2025-2026: Replit дропнул базу и бэкапы, сервис аренды машин ушатал прод.
• Multi-agent flow: refiner + архитектор + автономный бот, PR за час вместо недели.
• Тимлидам: не носи инженерам PR, которые ты навайпкодил за вечер.
• Что реально учить в 2026: Linux, сеть, Kubernetes, один язык программирования и AI-грамотность.
• Знать базу vs спрашивать AI: почему без фундамента ты не поймёшь, куда тебя модель направляет.

ГОСТЬ
В гостях - Андрей Волхонский, руководитель юнита System в Центре разработки инфраструктуры Авито. 13+ лет опыта: от Windows-DevOps в TravelLine и Kaspersky до платформенной инженерии в большой продуктовой компании.

videoTitle: DevOps in 2026: Stay in DevOps or Transition to MLOps, AIOps, DataOps?
videoDescription:
As we close out 2025, many DevOps engineers are facing the same question:
Should I continue growing in DevOps, or is it time to transition into MLOps, AIOps, or DataOps?

With AI agents and agentic workflows increasingly automating infrastructure and operations, it’s natural to wonder how these changes impact DevOps roles and career paths going into 2026.

In this video, I break down what’s actually changing — and what isn’t. You’ll get a clear, practical explanation of DevOps, MLOps, AIOps, and DataOps, how AI agents fit across all of these domains, and how to think about your career without chasing hype or fear-driven narratives.

What you’ll learn in this video:

Why DevOps is not dying, but evolving into specialized domains

The real difference between DevOps, MLOps, AIOps, and DataOps

Where AI agents and agentic workflows actually fit in operations

When it makes sense to stay in DevOps

When transitioning to MLOps, AIOps, or DataOps is the right move

Why these paths are not mutually exclusive

How to choose a direction based on the problems that genuinely excite you

This video is designed for engineers who want clarity, not clickbait — and who want to make career decisions grounded in real systems, real demand, and real interest.

If this helped you understand where the industry is heading, consider subscribing. In upcoming videos, I’ll go deeper into each specialization — DevOps, MLOps, AIOps, and DataOps — with real-world context and practical insights.

🚀 About This D365 Development Series
──────────────────────────

This series goes beyond basic tutorials to show you how real-world Dynamics 365 (D365FO) projects are built from start to finish. We'll build a complete, end-to-end "Automated Customer Tiering System" for a fictional client, Bluestone Industrial Components (BIC).

You'll see every step of a production-ready solution, from setup to deployment, covering:
➤ Core X++ Development: Extending tables and forms (CustTable), creating Enums, and implementing custom business logic using Chain of Command (CoC).
➤ Automation: Building robust, automated batch jobs with the SysOperation Framework.
➤ APIs & Integration: Creating Data Entities to build secure OData REST APIs and for Data Management Framework (DMF) exports.
➤ Event-Driven Architecture: Firing real-time alerts from D365 to Azure Logic Apps using Business Events.
➤ Business Intelligence: Connecting D365 to Power BI to build an interactive sales dashboard.
➤ DevOps & ALM: Setting up a complete CI/CD pipeline in Azure DevOps, managing source control (TFVC), and automating builds.

🔹Visual Studio 2019

videoTitle: The DevOps Godfather on AI's "Dark Factory" Problem
videoDescription:
Organizations are resisting the 'dark factory' model, not because of a lack of technological capability, but due to unprepared structures and mindsets. Coding agents are ready, but companies aren't set up for their seamless integration. Just like continuous delivery faced skepticism in 2009, autonomous coding agents now challenge existing frameworks and require a paradigm shift from developers as coders to orchestrators of systems. The shift isn't about better technology; it's about rethinking the roles and processes within an organization. Developers must evolve from technical craftsmanship to a conductor role in a system-driven environment, changing how teams and platforms function.

Patrick Debois, known widely as the 'godfather of DevOps', brings unique insights to this discussion. Having witnessed similar skepticism with the continuous delivery movement, Debois now observes the parallels between the challenges faced then and the resistance faced by the 'dark factory' approach today. At Tessl, where he observes first-hand the dynamics of adopting autonomous code agents, he highlights how this shift influences collaboration, team dynamics, and the role of platform teams.

What we cover:
• Why do organizations resist AI's 'dark factory' model?
• How do team dynamics change when developers become agent orchestrators?
• Which two metrics are crucial for measuring agentic productivity?
• What role do platform teams play in coding agent integration?
• How to hire for AI-native engineering roles
• Making a strong business case for adopting agent-driven engineering

videoTitle: Manage & Secure Kubernetes Cluster Policies via OPA Gatekeeper. #opa #devops #gatekeeper
videoDescription:
Manage & Secure Kubernetes Cluster Policies via OPA Gatekeeper. #opa #devops #gatekeepers 

Timestamps:

Theory/Concepts : 00:00
Hands on/Practical : 09:00

github repo : https://github.com/RohanRusta21/opa-gatekeeper.git

Concepts :

OPA Gatekeeper: Policy and Governance for Kubernetes

What is OPA:

The Open Policy Agent (OPA) is an open-source, general-purpose policy engine that unifies policy enforcement across the stack. OPA provides a high-level declarative language that lets us specify policies as code and simple APIs to offload policy decision-making from our software. We can use OPA to enforce policies in microservices, Kubernetes, CI/CD pipelines, API gateways, and more. 
In kubernetes, OPA uses admission controllers.

What is OPA Gatekeeper?

OPA Gatekeeper is a specialized project providing first-class integration between OPA and Kubernetes.
OPA Gatekeeper adds the following on top of plain OPA:
● An extensible, parameterized policy library.
● Native Kubernetes CRDs for instantiating the policy library (aka “constraints”).
● Native Kubernetes CRDs for extending the policy library (aka “constraint templates”).
● Audit functionality.

Why you need Gatekeeper?

As a Platform DevOps engineer managing multiple Kubernetes clusters for various projects, you face challenges when users deploy applications without adhering to best practices. Key issues include:
  1.     Lack of ownership unless users apply labels themselves.
  2.     No resource limits, leading to high costs.
  3.     Untrusted images impacting other applications.
  4.     Security and best practice violations across clusters.

To address these, we need governance to enforce limits and rules via policies. OPA Gatekeeper can be configured to implement these policies, ensuring best practices are followed.

Certifications for Employed DevOps Professionals:
AWS Certified DevOps Engineer: This certification from Amazon Web Services (AWS) validates your expertise in deploying, operating, and managing applications on the AWS platform.
Azure DevOps Engineer: Offered by Microsoft, this certification demonstrates your skills in designing and implementing DevOps practices using Azure technologies.
Google Cloud Professional DevOps Engineer: This certification focuses on designing, developing, and managing DevOps practices on the Google Cloud Platform.
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA): Certified by the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF), CKA validates your Kubernetes skills, which are crucial for container orchestration.
Certified Jenkins Engineer: Offered by CloudBees, this certification recognizes your proficiency in using Jenkins for continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines.
Red Hat Certified Engineer in DevOps: This certification from Red Hat validates your skills in using Red Hat technologies for automating, managing, and optimizing DevOps processes.

Courses for Aspiring DevOps Engineers:
Introduction to DevOps Practices: Online platforms like Coursera, edX, and Udemy offer various introductory courses that cover the fundamental concepts and practices of DevOps.
Docker and Kubernetes Courses: Understanding containerization and orchestration tools like Docker and Kubernetes is essential. There are numerous courses available for beginners and advanced users.
Cloud Platform Courses (AWS, Azure, GCP): Learning the basics of cloud platforms and their DevOps-related services is crucial. Many platforms offer free and paid courses for beginners.
CI/CD Pipeline Courses: Courses on continuous integration and continuous delivery tools like Jenkins, GitLab CI/CD, and CircleCI are essential for automating software delivery.
Infrastructure as Code (IaC) Courses: Learning tools like Terraform and Ansible for automating infrastructure deployment is key for DevOps engineers.
Monitoring and Logging Courses: Understanding tools like Prometheus, Grafana, and ELK Stack (Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana) for monitoring and logging is vital.
Scripting and Programming Courses: Proficiency in scripting languages like Python and programming languages like Java can enhance your DevOps skills.
Security and Compliance Courses: DevOps engineers should also be well-versed in security practices. Courses on DevSecOps and security automation can be beneficial.

Timestamp:
Understand Concept : 00:00
RabbitMQ Hands-on : 22:06

🧠 1. What Is RabbitMQ?

RabbitMQ is an open-source message broker — it acts as a middleman between different parts of a system that need to communicate asynchronously.
It uses the AMQP (Advanced Message Queuing Protocol) as its core protocol.

In simpler terms:

It receives messages from producers (applications sending data),

Stores them temporarily in queues,

And delivers them to consumers (applications receiving data).

This helps decouple systems — the sender and receiver don’t need to be active at the same time.

⚙️ 2. Why Use RabbitMQ?

✅ Decoupling – Producers don’t need to know who consumes messages.
✅ Asynchronous communication – Improves system responsiveness.
✅ Load balancing – Messages can be distributed across multiple consumers.
✅ Reliability – Ensures message delivery even if parts of the system fail.
✅ Scalability – You can add more queues or consumers easily.
✅ Flexible routing – Decide how messages flow using exchanges and routing keys.

🔩 3. Core RabbitMQ Concepts
🏭 Producers

Applications that send messages to RabbitMQ.
They don’t send messages directly to a queue but to an exchange.

🎯 Exchanges

An exchange routes messages to queues based on routing rules.

Exchange types:

Type Behavior Example Use Case
Direct Routes messages to queues whose binding key exactly matches routing key Task queues
Fanout Broadcasts all messages to all queues bound to it Notifications, pub/sub
Topic Routes messages based on pattern matching (* and #) Selective subscriptions
Headers Routes based on header attributes Advanced filtering

videoTitle: Salesforce Devops -- What Is Next? Dreamforce 2021
videoDescription:
DF 21 Inspiring Excellence 

Slides PDF with notes 
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a-bsFs1rY3ofUJrusbcW80Q7bcSym6Oy/view?usp=sharing

Slide 1
Welcome everyone to Dreamforce 21 Inspiring Excellence sessions. I’m Vernon Keenan from SalesforceDevops.net in Oakland, California. Let’s commit!
Slide 2
I’ve spent 2021 curating and cataloging the companies, products and services that help Salesforce customers deliver enterprise applications. Here is what I learned.
Slide 3
Let’s get our arms around DEVOPS. It seems to be the latest Salesforce buzzword. And it has turned into a powerful word indeed. 
If you are “doing devops” today that indicates you are managing how to build the means of production for your organization. If you want to exist as an enterprise in the digital domain, then you need devops to have the automation capabilities that delivers enterprise app updates and continuously improves app value.
The origin of the devops concept started in 2007 when its main push was to find ways to obliterate barriers between app developers and system operators. Developers became frustrated with the time it took to iterate on software builds when dealing with operations teams. 
This diagram from Azure DevOps website portrays it beautifully. It shows how better communication results in the collaboration and teamwork necessary to manage, develop, deliver and operate a live application. It shows the main benefit of using devops, which is to have a mechanism that allows teams to respond quickly to user behavior.
Another key to the success of DevOps is the idea of metrics and observability, and how that dovetails with agile management philosophies, such as tying metrics into objectives and key results. In fact, I’d say that Devops and Agile have been kissing behind the barn, and a new unified app production perspective is evolving which I call Devops 3.0.
Slide 4
One reason why devops has gained prominence is because it represents the convergence of three huge business forces. First, Salesforce is now a business transformation platform, and not just a CRM. Since the platform is strategic for many more businesses, executives need a governance harness and better visibility into app production activities.
Next, an all-pervasive force in modern information technology is the incredibly rich and diverse world of cloud native computing. When engineers at Uber, Salesforce, Netflix, or a new startup need tools to build an online service from scratch, they are using cloud native computing tools and services.
Until 2017, Salesforce was largely a closed platform to the cloud native world. Then SFDX-CLI was introduced and that really made Salesforce devops take off. It allowed LINUX scripts and cloud native tools to now interact with configuration information in Salesforce. That subsequently lets cloud native automation tools like Jenkins and Azure Devops act as a command server in a release management pipeline orchestration scheme. 
Slide 5
I made this relationship classification system to help figure out if all the boxes are checked when you are building an continuous app delivery system. This diagram gives you an idea of the complexity involved in a Salesforce devops solution. So, the good news is that we have good roadmaps for how to build a devops solution, but the bad news is that there are a lot of things to do and a lot of systems that need to be tied together.
That’s where a key software vendor like GEARSET comes into play. Salesforce devops platform vendors are all working to check these boxes off for you, so they are worth a look if you are getting started.
Slide 6
Now, let’s take that mess of products and reorganize them into this stack. This summary shows how Salesforce devops is first controlled by the governance functions, which collects metrics and data from the app production teams. Next, these teams of architects, developers, admins, business analysts, and constituents use a consistent set of automation and deployment tools to continuously optimize apps.
One key thing that makes this different for Salesforce app is the curious way in which we must manage metadata. A key function in Salesforce devops is that metadata must be ingested, analyzed, queried, and dynamically updated. When updating a live org, this is the only way for an app production team to work together. There must be intelligent metadata management in any Salesforce devops platform in order to optimize your release management processes. 
Slide 7
Now we are expanding the pyramid to show some of the functional layers in a full-fledged Salesforce devops solution, pretty much like what you get with Gearset. Here we can see some of the more familiar names and details that go into creating a full devops solution.

Slide 8
Now, let’s explode this out some more. Ben McCarthy of SalesforceBen and I worked together to design this Period Table of Devops Solutions,

videoTitle: The Difference Between DevOps Engineers, System Administrators, and IT Technicians (Desktop Support)
videoDescription:
After watching this video, you will find out who IT technicians, sysadmins, and system engineers are. Why is there so much hype around DevOps right now? How do engineers differ from administrators? And what highly specialized professions are system administrators divided into?

Timestamps:
0:00 Intro
1:07 IT technicians a.k.a. Desktop Support Engineers & Administrators
2:49 System Engineers & Administrators
4:38 Network Engineers & Administrators
6:07 Information Security Specialists a.k.a. Cyber Security Engineers
7:13 DevOps Engineers
9:27 Things To Remember

IT technicians (also known as Desktop Support Engineers) in most organizations are responsible for laptops, PBXs, printers, scanners, etc.

System engineers are responsible for complex IT systems design, and administrators work with the existing systems. Both are more about networks, servers, and other complex hardware.

In large organizations, the aspects of system administration are often divided into narrow specializations: networks, web administration, information security.

DevOps engineers are indispensable persons in companies with development teams and continuous integration (online games, streaming platforms, large retailers, and other services with an audience of thousands). They are responsible for smooth development, testing, and deployment.

videoTitle: What's the goal of Platform Engineering? #shorts #devops #platformengineering
videoDescription:
Watch the full video: https://youtu.be/JAblex0uS4k

What’s the goal of Platform Engineering? Platform Engineering focusses on the building the infrastructure and the systems that are needed for running your applications and supporting your application throughout the software life cycle. So,  the goal  is to support the developers in the organisation and treat them as customers. That’s why we have in platform engineering the concept of IDP Internal developer platform.
 
So, this platform is treated as an actual product and the customers of the product are the developers.
What is the role of the IDP?
It is to create a thin layer on top of the toolchain that is used inside the organisation to standardise the processes and help developers to have one way to deploy into production

videoTitle: Git Plumbing vs Porcelain #Git #GitHub #GitLab #BitBucket #DevOps #GitOps #Python #Java #JavaScript
videoDescription:
Have you heart the terms Git plumbing and Git Porcelain?

Ever wondered what the different between Git porcelain vs plumbing was?

For the most part, the porcelain is the most commonly used Git files such as:

- git init
- git add
- git commit
- git revert
- git merge
- git rebase
- git reset

That's the Git porcelain, and you won't get your hands too dirty when you touch it.

The Git plumbing? That's typically the config stuff in the hidden .git folder, including things like:

- Refspec
-Packfiles
- The HEAD Pointer
- Git References
- Remote References
- Transfer Protocols
- Garbage Collector
- Recovery files
- Tree Objects
- Environment variables

Hopefully you don't have to get your hands dirty with the Git plumbing too often. It's nice to stick with the Git porcelain.

But at the same time, plumbers do make a lot of money!

videoTitle: Stop using Read-Host and do this instead #powershell  #devops  #scripting

Stop using Read-Host and do this instead:

Read-Host has limitations. 

- You cannot pass information to it 
- You cannot validate what the user provided
- It always stops the script

There is a better way - use parameters instead.

- Control the type of input
- Make it mandatory or optional
- Pass argument from the command line
- or prompt the user to provide an argument, when required and not passed

videoTitle: Your /loop dies when you close the terminal
videoDescription:
/loop behaves differently depending on whether you give it an interval, a prompt, both or neither.

With an interval and a prompt, Claude converts the interval to a cron expression and runs your prompt on that fixed schedule. With a prompt only, Claude picks the gap itself, somewhere between one minute and one hour, and prints the delay and the reason at the end of each pass. With neither, it runs a built-in maintenance prompt: continue unfinished work, tend the pull request on your branch, then cleanup when nothing is pending.

All three land in the same scheduled task list, so you can list or cancel them the same way. Esc clears the pending wakeup while a loop is waiting.

The limit worth knowing: tasks only fire while Claude Code is running and idle. Closing the terminal or letting the session exit stops them. Backgrounding the session carries /loop tasks into a background session that keeps running without a terminal. Run /bg inside the session to do that, or press the left arrow on an empty prompt, which backgrounds it and opens agent view in one step. claude agents shows every background session on one screen.

/loop needs Claude Code 2.1.72 or newer.

videoTitle: Era of the DevOps Platform | GitKon 2022 | Brendan O’Leary, GitLab
videoDescription:
We’re in a new era of the DevOps platform. Hear from Brendan O’Leary, developer evangelist at GitLab as he shares his thoughts on how the industry is evolving. 

For years, operations teams have tried to build elastic compute platforms for developers to deploy to, while at the same time, developers were stitching together tools to ensure code was integrated, built, tested, and secure. In response, we’ve seen the DevOps industry move towards the era of DevOps platforms, consolidating and expanding capabilities that allow developers to spend more time on code and less on tools.

Brendan O’Leary, staff developer evangelist at GitLab, discussed the era of the platform, including how elite software delivery and operations performers are leveraging platforms like Kubernetes and the DevOps platform to adapt and ship code faster. To paraphrase Halt and Catch Fire: “Platforms aren’t the thing. They are the thing that gets you to the thing.”

videoTitle: What FinOps-Mature DevOps Leaders Do Differently (Cast AI)
videoDescription:
In this FinOps X 2026 lightning talk, Esmira Bayramova of Cast AI opens with a striking data point from analyzing 23,000+ Kubernetes clusters: only 8% of provisioned CPU, 20% of memory, and 5% of GPU actually get used.

Her core argument is that the waste isn't a cost problem, it's an ownership problem: immature teams treat cost as finance's job and review the bill retroactively once it's too late to act, while mature teams keep engineering in the room permanently, with one hard rule, no blame culture, and one real question, what did we ship per dollar?

She draws a direct line from the 2015-era "nobody thought about cloud cost until the bill exploded" story to the exact same pattern now playing out with AI and token spend, and makes the case that mature AI FinOps means tracking cost per outcome and value, not just cost per API call.

1:23 The reveal: 8% CPU, 20% memory, 5% GPU utilization across 23,000 clusters

7:14 Cloud era vs. AI era: the metrics that actually matter

videoTitle: Sysadmin to DevOps 2026: What Counts, What's the Gap
videoDescription:
Every DevOps roadmap says fifteen tools and two years. Your week is the load-bearing half of DevOps.

Run your own scan: https://scan.darrelldoesdevops.com

Five areas make up your week as a sysadmin, and every one maps straight across to DevOps. Same duties, different wrappers.

Administer → Linux and Git
Build → Terraform, CloudFormation, Bicep
Virtualize → Docker and Kubernetes
Script → GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab
Visibility → proof outside your own company

Change control sits under all of it, and on the DevOps side that's Git. Same discipline you already run, automated.

I came from the Windows side. My Linux was weak and I didn't understand Git at all. That's a short list, not a career restart. It still took me two years, because in 2018 I was spending my one hour a day hunting for this map instead of closing the gap.

The scan scores you on all five and hands back the two to work on next. Takes about two minutes. Noob means you know what it is, Mid means you've built something with it, Pro means you've run it enough times that it's boring.

You look at DevOps job postings, count forty tools, and quietly decide it's a two or three year project. It isn't. It's five areas, and you already own pieces of them if you came from ops.

I came from Windows and PowerShell, not Linux, and broke in the slow, scattered way before anyone drew me the map. So I drew it.

The real skill now isn't memorizing tools, and it isn't handing the work to AI either. It's using AI to learn faster while you do the reps yourself, until you understand the work well enough to catch the AI when it's wrong. That's the person who gets hired.

No faceless automation, no AI voice, no fifty-tool tutorials you'll forget by Friday. Just the map, the reps, and how to point AI at the parts you're stuck on.

videoTitle: Your 40GB copy has no progress bar. pv gives it one in 3 seconds
videoDescription:
A 40 GB copy, twenty minutes in, and not a single line of output. Is it working, or did it die? cp gives you nothing to go on — a slow copy and a hung process look identical.

Two things worth knowing beyond the basic case.

Dropped between two stages of a pipe, pv tells you which side is the bottleneck. If the rate is low with the dump on the left, the dump is your limit — not the compressor everyone blames first.

And pv -d PID attaches to a process that's already running. It reads the file offset out of /proc and draws the bar for a copy you started ten minutes ago without thinking. That works on cp, tar, dd — anything holding the file open.

Install: apt install pv / brew install pv

More practical engineering notes: https://www.alekseialeinikov.com/en/blog

videoTitle: LISTEN on :22 - and still refused
videoDescription:
ss says LISTEN on port 22. The daemon is up. The client still gets Connection refused.

  The port was never the whole answer — look at the address in front of it. 127.0.0.1 is loopback. A listening socket is
  bound to an address AND a port, not just a port, and a loopback socket is invisible to every other machine in the
  world.

  From the server, that very same daemon logs you straight in. Both results are correct, and that is what makes this one
  expensive. Nothing is broken, nothing logs an error, and the two people looking at it are both telling the truth.

  Don't grep for the port. Read the address.

  Full 10-minute walkthrough:
  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fzdNXFdCwV0

  Narration on this channel is synthesized. Everything shown on screen is a real session on a real machine — including
  the parts that fail.
